instruction.name: xvldx
instruction.description: Read whole vector from memory address `addr + offset`, save the data into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. Note that you can use this intrinsic to load floating point vectors, even though the return type represents integer vectors.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 250 --unroll2 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; addi.d $r23, $r20, 128; li.d $r4, 8; st.d $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.d $r4, $r20, 8' --asm 'xvldx $xr0, $r20, $r0; xvst $xr0, $r23, 0; ld.d $r4, $r23, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the 10.04-cycle store forwarding plus the add.d are subtracted, leaving the 4-cycle vector load.

latencies.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the store-to-load forwarding (10.04 cycles) and the add.d (1 cycle) are subtracted, leaving the 4-cycle vector load.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldx $xr0, $r20, $r4; xvldx $xr1, $r20, $r5; xvldx $xr2, $r20, $r6; xvldx $xr3, $r20, $r7; xvldx $xr4, $r20, $r8; xvldx $xr5, $r20, $r9; xvldx $xr6, $r20, $r10; xvldx $xr7, $r20, $r11
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, 0; li.d $r5, 32; li.d $r6, 64; li.d $r7, 96; li.d $r8, 128; li.d $r9, 160; li.d $r10, 192; li.d $r11, 224; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvldx $xr0, $r20, $r4; xvldx $xr1, $r20, $r5; xvldx $xr2, $r20, $r6; xvldx $xr3, $r20, $r7; xvldx $xr4, $r20, $r8; xvldx $xr5, $r20, $r9; xvldx $xr6, $r20, $r10; xvldx $xr7, $r20, $r11'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower.

notes: L1D-hit vector load latency is 4 cycles, the same as the scalar floating-point loads.
